_note: Indicative agronomic table for Uruguay (southern hemisphere). Kc values approximate FAO-56. Must be reviewed by a local agronomist. 'meses' = calendar months the crop occupies (sowing to harvest or termination); 'kc' has one value per month. 0-5 scores are relative between crops. User-facing text is in English.

cultivos.critico_por: flowering and grain fill, very sensitive to water shortage
riesgos: Soybean after soybean builds up root and stem diseases and pests such as stink bugs: check the paddock's history.
It leaves little stubble, so after harvest the soil is exposed to erosion.
vacios: Grain soybean adds little net nitrogen: most of it leaves the field with the grain.

cultivos.critico_por: late grain fill, which depends on February and March rain
riesgos: It is sown late, on the winter crop's stubble, so yield depends heavily on February and March rain.
If the winter crop is harvested late, sowing is delayed and yield potential drops.
vacios: Grain soybean adds little net nitrogen: most of it leaves the field with the grain.

cultivos.critico_por: flowering, very sensitive to heat and water shortage
riesgos: Very sensitive to heat and water shortage at flowering (December–January): review the sowing date, the hybrid and whether irrigation is possible.
It needs plenty of nitrogen: an agronomist should set the fertilizer plan.

cultivos.critico_por: flowering, although it handles heat and drought better than maize
riesgos: Grain sorghum suffers bird damage.
As forage it can poison cattle (prussic acid) when they graze young regrowth or right after a frost.

cultivos.critico_por: heading and flowering, sensitive to late frosts
riesgos: Late frosts at heading (October) can damage the grain.
Very wet springs favor Fusarium head blight.
Wheat after wheat increases stubble-borne diseases.
Malting barley is usually grown under contract with a malting company: confirm the market before sowing.
Sensitive to late frosts and to diseases in wet springs.
Its market and logistics are less developed than wheat's: confirm a buyer first.
Pods shatter easily, so harvest needs experience or suitable equipment.
Sensitive to frost at flowering.
It must be terminated on time (3–4 weeks before sowing the summer crop) so it doesn't take water from the next crop.
vacios: It produces no grain to sell: its value is protecting and improving the soil, which doesn't always show in a single year's income.

riesgos: Terminate it before it sets seed so it doesn't become a weed.
It fixes more nitrogen if left to grow until flowering, which can clash with the maize sowing date.
vacios: How much nitrogen it leaves varies a lot with how much it grows: it's worth measuring.

riesgos: It needs nitrogen fertilizer and good grazing management.
vacios: Its income comes through beef or milk, which the tool doesn't calculate.

cultivos.nombre: Mixed pasture (tall fescue, white clover, birdsfoot trefoil)
riesgos: It needs livestock, fences and water points: confirm the farm has them.
Establishment is the critical moment: an autumn drought can make it fail.
vacios: Its income comes through beef or milk, which the tool doesn't calculate.
